title: Only Mira runs the build
prompt:
`studio/build.sh` is executable by everyone. Change its permissions so that only its owner, Mira, may run it. Everyone may still read it, and only Mira may change it:

```
-rwxr--r--
```

Look at it with `ls -l studio` before and after.
hints: Read the permissions in three groups of three: owner, group, others.
In octal, read is 4, write 2 and execute 1, added up for each group.
check:
m=$(stat -c %a studio/build.sh)
if [ "$m" = 744 ]; then ok "studio/build.sh is -rwxr--r-- (744)."; else no "studio/build.sh is $(stat -c %a studio/build.sh) ($(stat -c %A studio/build.sh)), not -rwxr--r-- (744)."; fi
if [ "$(stat -c %U studio/build.sh)" = mira ]; then ok "Mira still owns it."; else no "Its owner changed; Mira should still own it."; fi

title: Pass through, but don’t look
prompt:
On a directory, read permission lets you list its names and execute permission lets you enter it and reach the files inside.

Change `studio/private` so that Mira keeps full access, while her group and everyone else may enter it but not list it: `drwx--x--x`. Don’t change the files inside.
hints: For the group and others you want only execute: that is 1 in octal.
The owner keeps read, write and execute: 7.
check:
m=$(stat -c %a studio/private)
if [ "$m" = 711 ]; then ok "studio/private is drwx--x--x (711)."; else no "studio/private is $(stat -c %a studio/private) ($(stat -c %A studio/private)), not drwx--x--x (711)."; fi
if [ "$(stat -c %a studio/private/ideas.txt)" = 600 ]; then ok "ideas.txt inside it is unchanged (600)."; else no "ideas.txt changed to $(stat -c %a studio/private/ideas.txt) ($(stat -c %A studio/private/ideas.txt)); leave the files inside as they were."; fi
if runuser -u jonas -- bash -c 'cd /home/mira/studio/private' 2> /dev/null; then ok "Jonas can enter it."; else no "Jonas can’t enter it: the others need execute permission."; fi
if runuser -u jonas -- ls studio/private > /dev/null 2>&1; then no "Jonas can still list it."; else ok "Jonas can’t list it."; fi

title: Take away the group’s write access
prompt: The folder `studio/art` belongs to Mira and the group `design`, and the group may write to it. Take away only the group’s write permission, and leave every other permission as it is, with a symbolic mode (letters, not digits). Don’t change `studio/art/hero.png`.
hints: Symbolic modes name who (`u`, `g`, `o`, `a`), an operator (`+`, `-`, `=`) and the permissions (`r`, `w`, `x`).
`-` takes permissions away and leaves the rest alone.
check:
m=$(stat -c %a studio/art)
if [ "$m" = 755 ]; then ok "studio/art is drwxr-xr-x (755): the group lost write and kept the rest."; else no "studio/art is $(stat -c %a studio/art) ($(stat -c %A studio/art)), not drwxr-xr-x (755)."; fi
if [ "$(stat -c %a studio/art/hero.png)" = 664 ]; then ok "hero.png is unchanged."; else no "hero.png changed to $(stat -c %a studio/art/hero.png) ($(stat -c %A studio/art/hero.png)). Change only the folder, without -R."; fi
